evidence.current_history: “The completed randomized study supports an insulation benefit on qualifying hot-route days”; “it does not validate the original pilot’s 40% claim.”
evidence.evidence_uncertainty: “risk ratio of 0.41 (95% CI 0.22–0.76)”; “recovered standardized records—16/80 versus 15/80—remain inconclusive, with potentially selective missingness.”
evidence.next_action: “A concurrent randomized study covering cooler weather would address generalizability.”

evidence.current_history: “The new trial supports a learning benefit from the combined offer for students with unreliable home internet”; “It does not vindicate the original causal claim.”
evidence.evidence_uncertainty: “0.24-standard-deviation benefit, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.10–0.38”; “The original assignment-based estimate—0.07 standard deviations, with a confidence interval of −0.08 to 0.22—also remains relevant.”
evidence.open_questions: “the trial cannot identify tutoring’s separate contribution or justify extending tutoring alone to every student”; “Their difference does not itself establish why attendance increased.”
evidence.next_action: “plan delivery of that offer with outcome monitoring”; “Broader expansion or removal of components warrants further randomized evaluation that directly tests those changes.”

evidence.current_history: “This resolves an important earlier uncertainty for that population and package”; “It does not vindicate the original 0.31-standard-deviation claim.”
evidence.evidence_uncertainty: “0.24-standard-deviation benefit (95% confidence interval, 0.10–0.38)”; “The original corrected invitation estimate—0.07 standard deviations, with a confidence interval of −0.08 to 0.22—remains the appropriate result for the original offer.”
evidence.open_questions: “the replication cannot isolate tutoring’s contribution or establish whether those supports are necessary”; “It also does not establish benefits for students with reliable internet.”
evidence.next_action: “Further randomized comparisons should examine tutoring alone versus the combined package and assess effects in broader student populations before universal expansion.”

evidence.current_history: “This resolves the earlier lack of a suitable hot-weather comparison”; “the pilot’s 40% exposure claim depended on operational alerts whose threshold changed during installation.”
evidence.evidence_uncertainty: “risk ratio of 0.41 (95% confidence interval 0.22–0.76)”; “recorded alerts and independently verified dispatch calls declined”; “device-related missingness limiting interpretation.”
evidence.open_questions: “effects in cooler weather remain unestablished”; “broader transfer remains unresolved.”
evidence.next_action: “Replace the dashboard’s” claim; “Extend randomized logger monitoring to cooler conditions if decisions require a year-round benefit estimate.”

evidence.current_history: “the package now has positive efficacy evidence”; “It does not vindicate the original tutoring offer.”
evidence.evidence_uncertainty: “0.24-standard-deviation benefit, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.10–0.38”; “The earlier 0.31 estimate came from a selective attendance comparison and remains unsuitable as a causal claim.”
evidence.open_questions: “the study cannot isolate tutoring’s contribution”; “The estimate concerns assignment to the package, not the effect of actually attending”; “These describe uptake but do not establish why attendance differed.”
evidence.next_action: “randomize tutoring alone and the combined package against ordinary support in the intended expansion population, retaining prespecified outcomes and analysis by assignment.”

evidence.current_history: “This resolves the earlier uncertainty about benefit in hot-route conditions”; “It does not validate the original pilot’s claimed 40% reduction.”
evidence.evidence_uncertainty: “risk ratio of 0.41 (95% CI 0.22–0.76)”; “recorded alerts fell from 30/120 to 18/120”; “selective missingness limits their interpretation.”
evidence.open_questions: “There are no new cool-weather data, so the hot-route result should not be generalized to all shipments.”
evidence.next_action: “a concurrent randomized comparison on cooler route-days using the same independent logging and prespecified endpoint, followed by an assessment of how benefits vary with temperature and the distributor’s route mix.”

evidence.current_history: “This is evidence of efficacy for that offer in that population”; “Its causal interpretation remains withdrawn.”
evidence.evidence_uncertainty: “assignment-based estimate is 0.24 standard deviations, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.10–0.38”; “The original randomized estimate—0.07 standard deviations, with a confidence interval of −0.08 to 0.22—remains useful evidence about the original invitation.”
evidence.open_questions: “the evidence cannot isolate tutoring’s contribution”; “Nor does it estimate the causal effect of actually attending”; “Their difference does not establish that the package caused higher attendance.”
evidence.next_action: “Further delivery of the studied package to comparable students is supported, with monitoring”; “a randomized comparison should test that offer in the intended population.”

evidence.current_history: “This resolves the earlier lack of a suitable hot-weather comparison”; “It does not validate the original pilot’s 40% exposure claim.”
evidence.evidence_uncertainty: “risk ratio is 0.41 (95% confidence interval 0.22–0.76)”; “The pilot still supports fewer recorded alerts and dispatch calls”; “remain inconclusive because of selective missingness and the before-and-after design.”
evidence.next_action: “examine whether benefits vary across measured hot-weather severity and routes, accounting for the blocked design”; “representative cool-weather comparisons are needed before extending the result to all shipments.”
